report.summary: (model supplied no summary; its answer is preserved in handoff)

handoff.purpose: Build a three-layer brief (symbols, imports with deep edges, documents) for a set of target files and their graph neighbourhood.

symbols.name: DEFAULT_BUDGET_CHARS
symbols.note: Default character budget for a whole brief, set to 12,000.

symbols.name: DEEP_EDGE_MARK
symbols.note: Marks an edge that exists only inside a function body; value is '*'.

symbols.name: ARTEFACT_ROOTS
symbols.note: Tuple of path prefixes considered artefacts: runs/, build/, dist/, .captures/.

symbols.name: _HEADER_RESERVE
symbols.note: Characters reserved for the header, set to 700.

symbols.name: _is_artefact
symbols.note: Returns True if rel starts with any ARTEFACT_ROOTS prefix.

symbols.name: GraphBrief
symbols.note: Frozen dataclass holding the rendered brief text plus targets, neighbours, counts, dropped, provenance.

symbols.name: GraphBrief.truncated
symbols.note: Property returning True if any dropped layer has a non-zero count.

symbols.name: _sig
symbols.note: Builds a signature string from an ast FunctionDef/AsyncFunctionDef node, including positional-only, vararg, kwonlyargs, kwarg.

symbols.name: file_symbols
symbols.note: Parses a Python file and returns top-level API declaration lines, including class methods one level down.

symbols.name: _deep_only_modules
symbols.note: Returns frozenset of dotted module names imported only inside function bodies.

symbols.name: _tail_matches
symbols.note: Checks whether any dotted name in a set plausibly denotes a given relative file path, by suffix matching.

symbols.name: _neighbourhood
symbols.note: BFS over edges and reverse edges from targets for up to hops steps, filtering artefacts and returning sorted neighbours.

symbols.name: graph_brief
symbols.note: Builds the brief for targets and their neighbourhood, using a supplied index or the cached_index; never raises for a missing/unreadable index.

claims.text: Three layers, which is why it is a brief and not a manifest: 1. symbols -- what exists, per file. Answers "does this name exist". 2. imports -- who reaches whom, INCLUDING the edges that live inside function bodies... 3. documents -- which page claims to describe this file.
claims.why: This chunk defines layer 1 (file_symbols) and layer 2 helpers (_deep_only_modules, _tail_matches), but layer 3 (documents) is not present in this chunk; the claim about its content cannot be verified here.

claims.text: Function-body edges are marked ``*``: 202 of 526 internal edges in this repo are only visible there, so a brief built from top-level imports alone would present ~60% of the graph as the whole of it.
claims.why: The numeric claims (202/526, ~60%) refer to a measured repository state not present in this chunk; the marking mechanism (DEEP_EDGE_MARK) exists but the actual edge data is not here.

claims.text: Layers 2 and 3 degrade cleanly: the type and document layers of the index are behind flags, and when they are off those sections are omitted rather than faked.
claims.why: The chunk shows no flag handling for layers 2 or 3; graph_brief has include_docs parameter but the body beyond line 1 is not shown, and layer 3 code is absent.

claims.text: What is never omitted silently is a TRUNCATION -- if the budget cuts the brief, the brief says what it dropped.
claims.why: The GraphBrief dataclass has a dropped field and a truncated property, but the actual rendering logic that would report dropped items is not in this chunk.

claims.text: This is a DERIVED artefact. It is regenerated, never edited, and a model must not cite it as evidence about behaviour -- it describes shape, not semantics.
claims.why: This is a policy claim about the module's usage; nothing in this chunk enforces or contradicts it.

claims.text: Default character budget for a whole brief. Sized from measurement, not taste: the full symbol layer for the ``daedalus/`` package is 6,479 characters, so a 1-hop brief around a handful of files fits comfortably and the budget only bites on a genuinely wide change.
claims.why: The measured 6,479 characters are not present in this chunk; the constant value 12,000 is defined but the measurement claim cannot be verified.

claims.text: Marks an edge that exists ONLY inside a function body. See the module docstring: this is the 38% of the import graph that naive tooling misses.
claims.why: The 38% figure is a measured statistic not present here; the constant is just a string '*'.

claims.text: Path prefixes that are ARTEFACTS, not the project, and must never appear in a brief. Both entries are measured, not defensive: ``runs/`` -- the first brief built for ``daedalus/shift.py`` listed ``runs/eval/deepseek_lab/wrecked/shift.py`` as a graph neighbour and printed its symbols... ``build/`` -- holds 142 stale copies of the package.
claims.why: The specific measured examples (runs/eval/..., 142 stale copies) are not present in this chunk; the constant tuple is defined but the measurement claims cannot be verified.

claims.text: Characters reserved for the header, which is composed after the layers are budgeted. Generous on purpose: overshooting the reserve wastes a few hundred characters, while under-reserving silently pushes the brief over the budget a caller sized its prompt against.
claims.why: The header composition logic is not in this chunk; only the constant value 700 is defined.

claims.text: Top-level API of one Python file, as declaration lines. Signatures rather than bare names... Methods are included one level down for classes... Deeper nesting is deliberately not listed -- it is not API.
claims.why: The function returns signature lines for top-level functions and classes, with methods one level down (indented with four spaces), and skips deeper nesting since it only iterates over class body directly.

claims.text: Dotted module names this file imports ONLY inside a function body. Computed here rather than read from the index because the index publishes a flat edge list with no depth: it correctly INCLUDES function-body edges (12 edges for ``offload.py`` against 7 top-level import statements -- verified), it just cannot say which ones they are. One extra AST pass over a handful of neighbour files buys the distinction.
claims.why: The specific example (offload.py, 12 edges vs 7 top-level) is not in this chunk; the function does compute deep-only modules by comparing top-level vs all-walk imports, but the measurement claim about the index cannot be verified here.

claims.text: Does any dotted name in the set plausibly denote ``rel``? Suffix matching on the dotted path, because a function-body import may be written ``from .kairos import drafts`` or ``import daedalus.kairos.drafts`` and both denote ``daedalus/kairos/drafts.py``. Over-matching here only ever adds a ``*`` mark to an edge that is genuinely present, so a wrong guess mislabels a true edge rather than inventing one.
claims.why: The function matches by suffix (last component or last two components) of the dotted name against the file path tail, which is consistent with the claim about over-matching only adding a mark to an existing edge, not inventing one.

claims.text: ``index`` may be supplied to avoid a rebuild; otherwise the process-wide cached index is used, which is single-flight, so two hundred concurrent lanes warm it once rather than each starting a full scan. That property is the difference between this being free and this being the reason a fan-out melts the box.
claims.why: The cached_index import and single-flight behaviour are mentioned in the code but the actual cached_index implementation is in another module; the single-flight property cannot be verified from this chunk.

claims.text: Never raises for a missing or unreadable index: a lane that cannot get a brief must still be able to run with none. A brief is context, not a gate.
claims.why: The try/except around cached_index is started in this chunk but the exception handling and the rest of the function are in the next chunk; the claim cannot be fully verified here.

observations.what: The module docstring makes several measurement claims (202/526 edges, 6,479 characters, 142 stale copies) that are not verifiable in this chunk; they are cited as measured but the data is not present.

file_symbols includes class methods one level down but skips dunder methods except __init__; this is a deliberate policy not mentioned in the docstring's 'one level down' claim but consistent with it.

_deep_only_modules computes deep imports by excluding top-level imports from all imports found via ast.walk; this correctly identifies function-body-only imports, but the docstring's claim about the index's flat edge list is unverifiable here.
_tail_matches uses suffix matching that could over-match (e.g., a module named 'drafts' matching any file named 'drafts.py'), but the docstring explicitly accepts over-matching as safe.
The graph_brief function begins with index resolution but the chunk cuts off mid-function; the 'never raises' claim cannot be fully checked.
